subject: Chemistry
title: The Element That Hid for 134 Years: Lanthanoid Contraction
summary: Hafnium sat in zircon beside zirconium but was found only in 1923, 134 years after zirconium, because the two are almost the same size (Zr 160 pm, Hf 159 pm) despite Hf's 32 extra electrons and extra shell. Between them in period 6 sit the 14 lanthanoids, across which the size of atoms and Ln³⁺ ions decreases steadily (La³⁺ ≈ 103 pm → Lu³⁺ ≈ 86 pm): the lanthanoid contraction. Each step adds a proton while the new electron enters 4f, which shields poorly (s > p > d > f), so the outer electrons are pulled in. The contraction cancels the expected increase in period 6: Zr ≈ Hf, Nb ≈ Ta, Mo ≈ W; Zr and Hf (and the lanthanoids) are hard to separate; and the basicity of Ln(OH)₃ decreases from La to Lu.
keyPoints: **Lanthanoid contraction**: the steady decrease in size of atoms and Ln³⁺ ions from La to Lu (La³⁺ ≈ 103 → Lu³⁺ ≈ 86 pm).
**Cause**: +1 proton each step while the new electron enters **4f**, which shields poorly (s > p > d > f).
**Zr ≈ Hf** (160 / 159 pm), Nb ≈ Ta, Mo ≈ W: the contraction cancels the extra shell of period 6.
Consequences: Zr/Hf and the lanthanoids are **hard to separate**; **basicity of Ln(OH)₃ decreases** La → Lu.

blocks.p: Why is Hf (Z = 72) almost the same size as Zr (Z = 40)? Going from period 5 to 6 adds a shell, which should increase the radius (as Ti 147 → Zr 160 pm). But the 14 lanthanoids come in between; each adds a proton and a poorly shielding 4f electron, so the size shrinks a little 14 times. The two effects nearly cancel: Hf is 159 pm.
